Held back by a tail of vague messages ('mega fix, idk what tho', 'Minor Update') and one 24,607-line pixel-2d scaffold commit that inflates raw volume.

executive_summary: Between 2024-08-30 and 2024-11-20 the team (223 commits, +74,670/-20,771) built a tournament platform of elo-ranking, gateway (RBAC), auth, user, matchmaking and tournament services plus a Vue frontend, using a PR-per-ticket workflow, solid unit/integration tests, good documentation and containerisation. Weaknesses: no CI/CD pipeline, patchy commit messages, workload concentrated in three contributors, and thin Jira/peer data (3 tickets, no peer evaluations).
strengths: Broad, working multi-service delivery with PR-per-ticket traceability
Substantial Java unit and integration test suite
Explicit documentation (elo README, Swagger) and full dockerisation
weaknesses: No CI/CD pipeline or automated checks
Vague commit messages and revert churn in places
Uneven workload; three handles with one or zero code commits
key_recommendations: Add a GitHub Actions (or equivalent) pipeline that builds, runs tests and builds Docker images on every PR.
Write real tests for auth, user and gateway and add a frontend test suite plus a coverage report.
Adopt a commit-message convention (ticket key + what changed) and stop one-line messages like 'mega fix'.
Keep Jira as the single source of truth: estimate every ticket and use one project key that matches commit references.
Rebalance work so the user/auth/frontend-lite contributors own tickets, and run peer evaluations each sprint.
